max_san.source_note: Keeper Rulebook p.167 (Sanity checklist F9): an investigator's maximum Sanity starts at 99 and is reduced by the investigator's Cthulhu Mythos score (current unmodified Cthulhu Mythos skill percentage). Maximum Sanity cannot exceed 99.

sample_loss_ladder.source_note: Keeper Rulebook p.155, sidebar 'Examples of Sanity Point Costs': twelve example situations in the book's order. The situation labels here are this repository's short paraphrases, not the book's sentences; the host offers these rows to Jev when a horror the module gives no number for is judged from what happened (contract §221.3).

rows.situation: surprised by a mangled animal carcass
surprised by a corpse or a body part
finding a horrifically mangled human corpse
meeting someone known to be dead
seeing a corpse rise from its grave
seeing a gigantic severed head fall from the sky

getting_used_to_the_awfulness.source_note: Keeper Rulebook p.169, 'Getting Used to the Awfulness': once an investigator has lost as many Sanity points to one sort of monster as that monster's maximum possible loss, no more is lost to it for a reasonable interval; every investigator development phase reduces each tracked total by 1. Investigators never truly get used to it (contract §221.6).

mythos_hardened.source_note: Keeper Rulebook p.169, optional rule 'Mythos Hardened': once Cthulhu Mythos rises above current Sanity, all later Sanity loss is halved; the change is permanent and does not revert if Sanity later exceeds Cthulhu Mythos (contract §221.7).

sanity_day.source_note: Keeper Rulebook p.156: the 'day' of the one-fifth indefinite-insanity rule is defined by the Keeper, usually lasting until the investigator reaches a place of safety and rests. The product closes it by the calendar day until a closed rest signal exists (contract §221.10).
